{{Short description|Characterizes complete connected Riemannian manifolds of constant curvature}}
In geometry, the '''Killing–Hopf theorem''' states that complete connected [[Riemannian manifold]]s of constant curvature are [[Isometry|isometric]] to a [[Quotient space (topology)|quotient]] of a [[sphere]], [[Euclidean space]], or [[hyperbolic space]] by a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] acting [[Group action (mathematics)|freely]] and [[Properly discontinuous action|properly discontinuously]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Lee |first=John M. |author-link=John M. Lee |date=2018 |title=Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds |url= |location=New York |publisher=Springer-Verlag |page=348 |isbn=978-3-319-91754-2}}</ref> These manifolds are called [[space form]]s. The Killing–Hopf theorem was proved by {{harvs|txt|last=Killing|authorlink=Wilhelm Killing|year=1891}} and {{harvs|txt|last=Hopf|authorlink=Heinz Hopf|year=1926}}.
